headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 H.B. 701 § 1). headings.title: Prohibition on mandatory employee microchip implantation

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for employer violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1883 merged with H.B. 2041). Declares any employer violating this section guilty of a class A misdemeanor. Independent review revised heading to specify employer violations.

headings.title: Definition of public safety employee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2020 1st Ex. Sess. H.B. 46, A.L. 2023 H.B. 402 merged with S.B. 24 merged with S.B. 186). headings.title: Bar on city residency requirement and permitted response time

headings.title: Establishment of Show-Me MyRetirement Savings Board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Establishes the "Show-Me MyRetirement Savings Board" in the office of the state treasurer.

headings.title: Board membership, chair, and appointment authorities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (5), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Designates the state treasurer or designee as chair and sets membership: state treasurer/designee, two senate-confirmed gubernatorial appointees with retirement-savings/investment and small-business expertise, three House members appointed by the speaker (including one minority-party member), and three Senate members appointed by the president pro tempore (including one minority-party member).

headings.title: Initial appointment terms beginning January 1, 2024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs the governor, senate president pro tempore, and house speaker to make their respective initial board appointments for terms beginning January 1, 2024.

headings.title: Appointed members serving at appointing authority's pleasure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Provides that board members appointed by the governor, senate president pro tempore, and house speaker serve at the pleasure of the appointing authority. Independent review revised heading to specify applicability to appointed board members.

headings.title: Four-year terms, reappointment, and filling vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Sets four-year terms of office, permits reappointment, and directs the appropriate appointing authority to make immediately effective appointments to fill vacancies for unexpired terms.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and travel expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Provides that board members serve without compensation and receive reimbursement from the administrative fund for necessary travel expenses incurred in board duties.

headings.title: Quorum requirement for board business
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Establishes that a majority of voting board members constitutes a quorum to transact business.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all seven subsections, subdivisions (1)–(5), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75); verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Plan design, development, implementation, and feasibility analyses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs the board, subject to §§ 285.1000 to 285.1055, to design, develop, and implement the plan and authorizes market, legal, and feasibility analyses.

headings.title: Fiduciary status and enumerated board powers and duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (23) and nested paragraphs, and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). headings.title: Prohibited financial interests, borrowing, and guarantees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Prohibits board members, the program administrator, and board staff from having direct or indirect interests in program investments or profits, borrowing or using program funds or deposits, or becoming an endorser, surety, or obligor on program investments.

headings.title: Board member conflict rules under sections 105.452 and 105.454
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Subjects each board member to §§ 105.452 and 105.454. headings.title: Plan name, adoption, and federal compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs the board to adopt and implement the "Show-Me MyRetirement Savings Plan" consistent with federal law and regulation and maintain federal compliance once implemented.

headings.title: Required and permitted plan features and administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (20), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Specifies 20 plan requirements and discretionary features under board terms and regulations: plan documents, voluntary participation by eligible employers, self-employed individuals, and qualifying associations, at-will participant termination, pretax/Roth 401(k) and employer contributions, board oversight and professional administration, optional uniform 1% annual contribution-rate escalation up to federal limits, direct deposit and ERISA-consistent investment options (target date default, principal-protected option, at least four alternatives, optional temporary security corridor), quarterly reports and online access, pooled arrangements, participant account ownership without state/employer proprietary interest, non-employee participation if federally allowed, distribution/fixed-income options, participant-initiated tax-exempt rollovers, and encouraging employer retirement plans.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections, all 20 subdivisions of subsection 2, and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75); verified all fingerprints. headings.title: No guaranteed returns and disclaimer of liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Provides that the state, board, members, other state officials/agencies/personnel, and plan do not guarantee any interest rate, rate of return, or investment performance and are not liable for any loss, deficiency, tax consequence, or loss of favorable tax treatment, public assistance, or other benefits from plan participation.

headings.title: Plan and board obligations not state debts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). States that debts, contracts, and obligations of the plan or board are not state debts, contracts, or obligations and that neither state faith and credit nor taxing power is pledged.

headings.title: Construction rule against return guarantees under sections 285.1000 to 285.1055
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs that nothing in §§ 285.1000 to 285.1055 shall be construed to guarantee any interest rate, rate of return, or investment performance on contributions or account balances.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all three subsections, subdivisions (1)(1)–(2), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75); verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Confidentiality of participant account information and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Requires individual account and participant information to remain confidential, subject to permitted disclosure to the extent necessary to administer the plan under §§ 285.1000 to 285.1055, ERISA, the IRC, or federal/Missouri law, or upon express written agreement by the providing or subject individual.

headings.title: Closed-record status under section 610.010
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Classifies information confidential under subsection 1 as a closed record under § 610.010 regardless of whether disclosed as allowed under subsection 1.

headings.title: Administrative fund creation, custody, and appropriation-limited use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Creates the "Show-Me MyRetirement Savings Administrative Fund" in the state treasury with the state treasurer as custodian, authorizes disbursements under §§ 30.170 and 30.180, and restricts distributions—subject to appropriation—solely to administering §§ 285.1000 to 285.1055.

headings.title: Exemption from biennial reversion under section 33.080
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Exempts end-of-biennium fund balances from reverting to the general revenue fund notwithstanding § 33.080.

headings.title: Investment of administrative fund moneys and earnings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs the state treasurer to invest administrative fund moneys like other funds and credit investment interest and earnings to the fund.

headings.title: Sources of moneys in the administrative fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, including subdivisions (1) through (6), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Enumerates fund sources: general assembly appropriations, federal/state/local transfers, fees and other moneys due to the board, gifts/donations/grants, legally permitted collections from plan contributions/returns/assets, and fund earnings.

headings.title: Acceptance of grants, gifts, and appropriations for the fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs the board, to the extent consistent with ERISA, tax qualification rules, and federal law, to accept grants, gifts, appropriations, or other moneys from public or private entities solely for deposit in the administrative fund. Independent review revised heading to remove "external" because the source explicitly includes the state alongside federal, local, and private entities.

headings.title: Start-up borrowing and long-term procurement contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Until account fees make the plan self-sustaining, authorizes the board to borrow working capital solely in the name of the plan and board payable exclusively from plan revenues, and to enter long-term procurement contracts with fee structures minimizing borrowing or state-asset reliance.

headings.title: Initial state administrative funding and repayment rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Permits the state, subject to appropriation, to pay administrative costs until fund assets suffice, after which all costs and state start-up repayments are paid solely from the fund; private or federal implementation funds need not be repaid unless conditioned on a repayment promise.

headings.title: Permitted administrative uses of fund moneys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Authorizes the board to use administrative fund moneys solely to pay plan administrative costs and expenses and board administrative costs and expenses under §§ 285.1000 to 285.1055.

headings.title: Competitive bidding for contractors and Office of Administration assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9, including subdivisions (1) and (2) and the closing continuation paragraph, and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Requires the state treasurer's office to follow Office of Administration competitive bidding for five-year program-management contracting and optional qualified-staff contracting upon reaching 50,000 participants, and authorizes the Office of Administration to provide necessary assistance and services.

headings.title: Accounting records, annual CPA audit, and auditor authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). headings.title: Annual August 1 public and audited financial report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Requires an annual August 1 public report to the governor, state treasurer, senate president pro tempore, and house speaker containing a GAAP audited financial report and detailed prior-year participation, contribution, withdrawal, asset, investment, fee, expense, and current-year projected activity summaries.

headings.title: Contribution start deadline of September 1, 2025
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Directs the board to establish the plan so individuals can begin contributing on or before September 1, 2025.

headings.title: Discretionary phased implementation and completion deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75). Permits the board to phase in contribution start dates by class of individuals, employer size or type, or non-employees, provided staged implementation is substantially completed on or before September 1, 2025.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 20 merged with S.B. 75); verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Definition of ride-sharing arrangement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Defines "ride-sharing arrangement" as transporting a fixed group in a vanpool between abode or nearby terminal and employment in a single daily round trip when the driver is also commuting.

headings.title: Workers' compensation exclusion and employer-vehicle exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Excludes injuries suffered during ride-sharing between residence/nearby terminal and employment from chapter 287 workers' compensation unless the employer owns, leases, or contracts for the vehicle.

headings.title: Employer liability exclusion for non-employer vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Exempts employers from liability for passenger or third-party injuries resulting from operating or using a ride-sharing vehicle not owned, leased, or contracted for by the employer.

headings.title: Employer liability exclusion for encouraging ride-sharing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Exempts employers from liability for passenger or third-party injuries based on providing information, incentives, or other encouragement for employee ride-sharing.

headings.title: Prohibition on special local taxes on ride-sharing vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Prohibits counties and municipalities from imposing a special tax applicable solely to a motor vehicle used in a ride-sharing arrangement.

headings.title: Default exclusion of ride-sharing travel from work hours
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Provides that commuting in an employer-sponsored ride-sharing arrangement is not part of an employee's work hours unless otherwise agreed to by the employer. Independent review revised heading to reflect the "unless otherwise agreed to by the employer" qualification.

headings.title: Public employee use of government vehicles and cost fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Permits state or local agency motor vehicles to be used in public-employee ride-sharing notwithstanding other law and requires participants to pay a fee reimbursing acquisition, operation, depreciation, and insurance costs.

headings.title: Vanpool registration, license plates, and agency-vehicle exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6). Directs the director of revenue to issue a distinctive vanpool license plate under § 301.066 and requires all ride-sharing vehicles—except state or local agency vehicles—to register as vanpools and bear the plate. Independent review revised heading to include the state and local agency vehicle exception.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all eight subsections and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 149, et al. & 517 § 6); verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 287 exclusion and employer-vehicle exception, employer tort exclusions, local special-tax bar, agreement exception to work-hours exclusion, public-vehicle reimbursement fees, and § 301.066 vanpool plate exception for agency vehicles. Retained subsections 1–5 and 7; revised subsections 6 and 8 to reflect the agreement and agency-vehicle exceptions.

headings.title: Definition of transient employer and specific exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1988 S.B. 488 § 1 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Defines "transient employer" for this section (non-Missouri domiciled employer under §§ 143.191, 287.030, and 288.032 temporarily transacting business not reasonably expected to continue 24 consecutive months), excludes employers exempt from Missouri income tax under 15 U.S.C. § 381, and includes nonresident professional athletic teams and entertainers unless the payer complied with § 143.183 for a nonresident entertainer.

headings.title: Financial assurance exemption for qualifying contiguous-state employers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and source notes. Exempts qualifying contiguous-state county employers with >=60 cumulative contract days per 12 months in each of the two preceding calendar years who hold DOR and DES tax clearances (noting the historical 90-day post-August 13, 1988 initial clearance rule and annual January 31 renewal requirement), specifies immediate loss of exemption on noncompliance or relocation, and preserves applicability of subsection 5.

headings.title: Required financial assurance instrument, amount, and conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Requires transient employers to file with the director of revenue a cash bond, surety bond, or § 400.5-103 irrevocable letter of credit (minimum $5,000, maximum $25,000, at least average estimated quarterly withholding tax) with licensed/approved surety and specified obligor/obligee conditions covering chapters 143, 287, and 288 compliance.

headings.title: Using contract-required financial assurance and tax clearance release
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Allows transient employers to satisfy the section using an existing contract-required financial assurance covering state and withholding taxes if delivered by certified mail by the awarding entity >=14 days before contract execution, subject to DOR director 14-day review (waived if no notice) and tax clearance prior to release.

headings.title: Certification of workers' compensation insurance or self-insurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Requires transient employers to certify sufficient workers' compensation coverage to the director of revenue via § 287.280 division-approved self-insurance or a policy in a contract form approved by the department of commerce and insurance.

headings.title: Replacement of discharged, reduced, or unsatisfactory financial assurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes. Authorizes the director of revenue to require a replacement financial assurance instrument if liability is discharged or reduced or a surety/financial institution becomes unsatisfactory, with release of the prior surety/institution upon satisfaction of accrued liability.

headings.title: Sixty-day surety release and employer replacement requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes. Releases a surety or financial institution from future liability 60 days after lodging a written release request with the director of revenue without relieving accrued or interim liability, requires prompt DOR notice to the employer, and requires the employer to file a replacement instrument within the 60-day period. Independent review revised heading to reflect the employer's 60-day replacement filing requirement.

headings.title: Additional financial assurance for tax delinquency or bad check
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes. Authorizes the director of revenue, notwithstanding the statutory amount cap, to demand an additional financial assurance instrument upon tax delinquency or an insufficient-funds tax check, subject to a combined penal sum limit of two quarters' estimated tax liability.

headings.title: Twenty-five percent deficiency addition for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes. Adds an additional 25% of any assessed deficiency—beyond other additions, interest, and penalties—for any period a transient employer fails to meet section requirements.

headings.title: Criminal offense of knowingly failing to file financial assurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes. Establishes that a taxpayer commits the crime of failure to file a financial assurance instrument by knowingly failing to comply with this section.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification and corporate fine limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and source notes (including footnote * noting "Section 560.021 was repealed by S.B. 491, 2014, effective 1-01-17"). Classifies failure to file a financial assurance instrument as a class A misdemeanor and states corporate fine authority up to $5,000 or twice the offense profit under archived reference to § 560.021*.

headings.title: Bar on contract performance before registration and financial assurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and source notes. Prohibits an employer who fails to register with DOR and execute the required financial assurance before starting a contract from performing on the contract until complying.

headings.title: Payroll recordkeeping, inspection, and one-year in-state retention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and source notes. Requires full and accurate payroll records (names, occupations/crafts, hours, actual wages) open to DOR inspection at reasonable times and retained undestroyed within Missouri for one year after contract completion.

headings.title: Secretary of state as registered agent for service
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and source notes. Deems entering a Missouri work contract an appointment of the secretary of state as registered agent for service of process, notice, or demand with the same legal force as personal service within the state.

headings.title: One-year public works bar for unfiled financial assurance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and source notes. Imposes an additional one-year prohibition from contracting for or performing labor on any Missouri public works project on employers failing to file a required financial assurance instrument. Independent review revised heading to state the unfiled financial assurance trigger.

headings.title: Ten-day written notice before discontinuing in-state activity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 16 and source notes. Requires a transient employer ceasing in-state activity to notify the director of revenue in writing at least 10 days before discontinuance takes effect.

headings.title: Inapplicability to out-of-state businesses under sections 190.270 to 190.285
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 17 and source notes (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Exempts out-of-state businesses operating under §§ 190.270 to 190.285 from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all 17 subsections, subdivisions (2)(1)–(3), history note (L. 1988 S.B. 488 § 1 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190), and footnote * noting repeal of § 560.021 by S.B. 491, 2014 effective 1-01-17; verified all fingerprints. Checked 15 U.S.C. § 381 and § 143.183 exclusions, contiguous-state exemption and August 13, 1988 / January 31 timelines, § 400.5-103 and § 287.280 cross-references, subsection 11 repealed-section note without enforceability claims, and subsection 17 out-of-state business exclusion under §§ 190.270 to 190.285.
