headings.title: Building permit prerequisites, injunctions, payment distribution, and local immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 472, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Requires political subdivisions issuing building permits to obtain § 285.230 tax clearance and financial assurance proof from transient employers; directs DOR to seek TRO/injunctive relief for missing/fraudulent proof or §§ 285.230 to 285.234 violations; permits equitable court distribution of due payments and breach-free hiring of a replacement contractor; and disclaims city or county liability for license issuance.

headings.title: Construction contractor verification, payment withholding, and immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 472, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Requires construction contractors to obtain DOR financial assurance and workers' compensation/self-insurance proof from transient subcontractors before work (with an exception if already submitted to a contracting state agency or political subdivision), mandates payment withholding upon written DOR or DWC director notice of §§ 285.230 to 285.234 violations, and provides contract/timely-payment compliance and civil/criminal immunity. Note source discrepancy retained verbatim in archived text: an incomplete duplicated sentence ("Any contractor withholding payment and paying such funds in satisfaction of the subcontractor's obligations as a transient employer if so directed by the director of revenue or the director of the division of workers' compensation.") precedes the complete immunity sentence. Independent review revised heading from "General contractor" to "Construction contractor" to match the opening applicability to any private or public construction contractor; verified verbatim retention of the duplicated incomplete sentence.

headings.title: Publication and monthly updates of transient construction contractor list
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 472, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Directs DOR, notwithstanding § 32.057, to submit a list of known transient construction contractors to the Missouri Register at least quarterly, update it monthly, and provide it free upon request.

headings.title: Inapplicability to out-of-state businesses under sections 190.270 to 190.285
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Exempts out-of-state businesses operating under §§ 190.270 to 190.285 from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all four subsections and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 472, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190); verified all fingerprints. Checked building-permit prerequisites, local immunity, § 32.057 list publication override, subsection 4 out-of-state business exclusion under §§ 190.270 to 190.285, and verbatim retention of the duplicated incomplete sentence in subsection 2 without silent repair. Retained subsections 1, 3, and 4; revised subsection 2 to cover any construction contractor rather than only general contractors.

headings.title: Escrow requirements and funding penalty for political subdivision contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 80 § 2, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Requires transient employers lacking conclusive § 285.230 compliance proof to escrow 20% of labor costs (or 10% of contract amount if not separately stated) with contracting political subdivisions for DOR, DES, or DWC tax liabilities with remainder refunded, and bars noncomplying political subdivisions from state public works funds for one year from discovery.

headings.title: Escrow requirements and tax liability for private entity contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 80 § 2, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Imposes the same 20% labor / 10% contract escrow and refund framework for private-entity contracts (retaining archived source phrasing "transient employers' contract") and makes a noncomplying private entity liable for full state withholding, workers' compensation, and employment security tax liabilities from the contract.

headings.title: Attachment and injunctive remedies for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 80 § 2, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Subjects transient employers failing to post financial assurance or escrow funds to a chapter 521 writ of attachment or other injunctive relief in addition to other remedies.

headings.title: Inapplicability to out-of-state businesses and employees under 190.270 to 190.285
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Exempts out-of-state businesses or out-of-state employees operating under §§ 190.270 to 190.285 from this section (noting inclusion of out-of-state employees, unlike §§ 285.230, 285.232, and 285.234).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all four subsections and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 80 § 2, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190); verified all fingerprints. Checked 20%/10% escrow rules and penalties for political subdivisions and private entities (retaining archived "transient employers' contract" phrasing), chapter 521 attachment remedy, and subsection 4's broader exclusion of both out-of-state businesses and out-of-state employees under §§ 190.270 to 190.285. Retained all four headings as accurate.

headings.title: Work-site posting of withholding, workers' compensation, and unemployment notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 626 § 1, A.L. 1997 H.B. 472, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Requires every transient employer under § 285.230 to post prominently and legibly at the work site copies of its DOR withholding registration notice, signed and DOR/DWC-verified workers' compensation coverage/self-insurance proof, and DES unemployment insurance registration notice.

headings.title: Daily penalty for failing to post required notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 626 § 1, A.L. 1997 H.B. 472, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Imposes a $500-per-day penalty on transient employers until required work-site notices are posted. Independent review revised heading to remove "civil" because the source text states "a penalty" without that modifier.

headings.title: Inapplicability to out-of-state businesses under sections 190.270 to 190.285
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190). Exempts out-of-state businesses operating under §§ 190.270 to 190.285 from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all three subsections, subdivisions (1)(1)–(3), and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 626 § 1 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1190); verified all fingerprints. Checked § 285.230 posting items, $500 daily penalty phrasing, and subsection 3 out-of-state business exclusion under §§ 190.270 to 190.285. Retained subsections 1 and 3; revised subsection 2 to remove unstated "civil" modifier.

headings.title: Veteran priority system in federally funded employment and training programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 385 § 2). Requires state-administered federally funded employment and training programs (retaining archived statutory reference to the Job Training Partnership Act, 29 U.S.C. § 1501) to include a veteran priority system preferring disabled veterans, target-specific veterans, other veterans, and other eligible persons over nonveterans within targeted groups. Independent review revised heading to include both employment and training programs.

headings.title: Order of referral priority for qualified applicants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (5), and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 385 § 2). Sets the five-tier state-agency referral order for subsection 1 job openings and training opportunities: special disabled veterans, target-specific veterans, all other veterans, other eligible persons, and nonveterans.

headings.title: Annual legislative and veterans commission service reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 385 § 2). Requires agencies providing subsection 1 employment and training services to submit an annual report to the House speaker, Senate president pro tem, and Missouri Veterans Commission chairman detailing entitlement and employment/training services by subsection 2 class plus a separate veterans reporting module.

headings.title: Mandatory state agency service and referral duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, including subdivisions (1) through (5), and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 385 § 2). Directs agencies administering subsection 1 programs to ensure courteous treatment at state facilities, prioritize job referrals and training enrollment for qualified veterans and eligible persons, give special disabled veterans preferential treatment in needed state services, and provide interagency benefit/service referral assistance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all four subsections, subdivisions (2)(1)–(5) and (4)(1)–(5), and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 385 § 2); verified all fingerprints. Checked archived 29 U.S.C. § 1501 (Job Training Partnership Act) reference, five-tier referral priority order, annual reporting recipients/modules, and state agency duties. Revised subsection 1 to include training programs alongside employment programs; retained subsections 2–4.

headings.title: Permissive private-employer veteran hiring and promotion preference
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 573). Permits a private, nonpublic employer to grant preference to a veteran in hiring and promoting employees. Independent review revised heading to specify private, nonpublic employer scope.

headings.title: Permissive preference for spouses of disabled or deceased veterans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 573). Permits a private, nonpublic employer to grant hiring and promotion preference to the spouse of a veteran with a service-connected permanent and total disability or the surviving spouse of a deceased veteran, and defines "disabled veteran" retaining the archived reference to the "United States Veterans Administration" or an armed forces retirement board. Independent review revised heading to reflect the permissive nature of the preference; verified embedded "disabled veteran" definition and archived "United States Veterans Administration" reference.

headings.title: Safe harbor under state equal employment opportunity laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 573). Clarifies that granting preferences under subsections 1 and 2 does not violate any state equal employment opportunity law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all three subsections and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 573); verified all fingerprints. Checked private, nonpublic employer scope, permissive "may grant" wording, embedded "disabled veteran" definition retaining archived "United States Veterans Administration" reference, and state EEO safe harbor. Revised subsections 1 and 2 to capture private-employer scope and permissive nature; retained subsection 3.

headings.title: New-hire W-4 reporting, state directory, and unemployment cross-checks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 253 § 19, A.L. 1997 S.B. 361, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1268 & 1211, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision). Requires employers to have newly hired employees complete W-4 forms and submit them (or § 285.304 equivalents) to DOR within 20 days of hire (as defined) or via semi-monthly electronic/magnetic transmissions; directs weekly DOR forwarding to the family support division for the State Directory of New Hires and federally required sharing (including 42 U.S.C. § 653 National Directory); and directs DES to cross-check unemployment compensation applicants/recipients weekly against federal new-hire/wage and SSA databases and, effective January 1, 2007, at least monthly against DOR driver's license databases.

headings.title: Multi-state employer electronic reporting designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 253 § 19 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision). Allows employers with employees in two or more states who transmit reports magnetically or electronically to comply with subsection 1 by designating one state of employment for transmissions and notifying the U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections, subdivisions (2)(1)–(2), and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 253 § 19 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision); verified all fingerprints. Checked W-4/§ 285.304 reporting timelines, 42 U.S.C. § 653 National Directory sharing, DES weekly federal/SSA and post-January 1, 2007 monthly DOR driver's license cross-checks, and multi-state electronic designation. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Submission of federal 1099 miscellaneous forms by qualifying employers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al.). Requires employers doing business in Missouri with five or more employees to submit applicable federal 1099 miscellaneous forms to DOR within Missouri Form 99 filing timelines.

headings.title: Fines for repeated intentional failures to report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al.). Authorizes a fine of up to $200 per failure on or after the fifth occurrence when an employer intentionally fails to submit subsection 1 information on five or more occasions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al.); verified all fingerprints. Checked five-employee threshold, Missouri Form 99 timeline reference, and five-occurrence intentional-failure penalty trigger. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Definition of knowing worker misclassification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al.). Establishes that an employer knowingly misclassifies a worker by failing to claim the worker as an employee while knowing the worker is an employee.

headings.title: Attorney general investigation and subpoena powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al.). Authorizes the attorney general to investigate alleged or suspected violations of §§ 285.500 to 285.515 with all investigative powers under §§ 407.040 to 407.090 and to serve and enforce related subpoenas.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al.); verified all fingerprints. Checked knowing misclassification standard and attorney general investigative/subpoena powers under §§ 285.500 to 285.515 and §§ 407.040 to 407.090. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibition on knowingly employing unauthorized aliens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390, A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Prohibits any business entity or employer from knowingly employing, hiring for employment, or continuing to employ an unauthorized alien to perform work within Missouri.

headings.title: Affidavits for public contracts, grants, incentives, and emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390, A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Requires sworn affidavits and documentation of federal work authorization participation and non-employment of unauthorized aliens for state/political subdivision contracts or grants exceeding $5,000 or state tax credits, abatements, or loans; limits public-contract affidavit filings to annually; and suspends enrollment/participation requirements for 15 working days during or immediately after a defined natural or manmade emergency. Independent review revised heading to include the 15-working-day emergency suspension alongside public contracts, grants, and incentives.

headings.title: Mandatory work authorization participation by public employers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Requires all public employers to enroll and actively participate in a federal work authorization program.

headings.title: Voluntary employer participation, record retention, and affirmative defense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Permits employers to enroll in a federal work authorization program, requires verifying post-enrollment hires and retaining dated federal verification reports, and provides participating business entities an affirmative defense to subsection 1.

headings.title: Contractor and subcontractor liability and investigation cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390, A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511; footnote * noting 'Section "285.252" appears in original rolls, which does not exist' for "sections 285.525* to 285.555"). Makes general contractors or subcontractors of any tier liable under §§ 285.525 to 285.555 for a direct subcontractor's subsection 1 violation when having knowledge under 8 CFR 274a.1, and requires full cooperation—including site access, employment files, contracts, and records—upon attorney general notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all five subsections, history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2009 H.B. 390, A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511), and footnote * on subsection 5 noting 'Section "285.252" appears in original rolls, which does not exist'; verified all fingerprints. Checked $5,000 public-contract/grant and incentive affidavit rules, 15-working-day emergency suspension, public-employer mandate, voluntary-enrollment affirmative defense, and 8 CFR 274a.1 contractor liability/cooperation. Revised subsection 2 to include emergency suspension; retained subsections 1 and 3–5.

headings.title: Attorney general enforcement authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Directs the attorney general to enforce §§ 285.525 to 285.555.

headings.title: Investigative powers and sworn complaint affidavit requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Authorizes attorney general investigation of alleged or suspected violations of §§ 285.500 to 285.515 and grants §§ 407.040 to 407.090 powers for investigating §§ 285.525 to 285.555 (explicitly retaining the archived source text's dual statutory ranges without silent alteration), and requires complaints under §§ 285.525 to 285.555 to be accompanied by a sworn affidavit under penalty of perjury.

headings.title: State burden of proof and work-authorization affirmative defense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Places a preponderance-of-the-evidence burden on the state to prove knowing employment of an unauthorized alien in Missouri and grants an affirmative defense to employers participating in a federal work authorization program.

headings.title: Injunctions, wage-based damages, state license suspension, and venue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Authorizes the attorney general to seek injunctions, monetary damages equal to ten times wages paid to unauthorized alien workers, and court suspension of state-issued business licenses, permits, or exemptions (including SOS or DOR), in circuit court where the violation occurs or in Cole County circuit court.

headings.title: Judgments, consent judgments, and local license suspensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Directs court entry of judgment and penalties consistent with the petition upon finding knowing hiring, authorizes attorney general consent judgments, and empowers the court and attorney general to direct municipal or county governing bodies to suspend applicable licenses, permits, or exemptions.

headings.title: Immunity under sections 285.525 to 285.555 for reporting employers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511). Exempts any employer reporting an alleged violation of §§ 285.525 to 285.555 to the attorney general from liability under those sections. Independent review revised heading to preserve the exact statutory scope of immunity under §§ 285.525 to 285.555.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all six subsections and history note (L. 2008 H.B. 1549, et al., A.L. 2026 H.B. 2366 & 2511); verified all fingerprints. Checked subsection 2's archived dual statutory-range wording (§§ 285.500 to 285.515 alongside §§ 285.525 to 285.555) and sworn-affidavit requirement, preponderance burden and affirmative defense, state versus local license suspensions, Cole County venue, and exact §§ 285.525 to 285.555 immunity scope in subsection 6. Retained subsections 1–5; revised subsection 6 to specify exact statutory immunity scope.

headings.title: Short title as Whistleblower's Protection Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Designates § 285.575 as the "Whistleblower's Protection Act".

headings.title: Section definitions and coverage exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (5) and paragraphs (a) and (b), and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Defines "because"/"because of", "employer" (six or more employees across 20+ weeks, excluding the state, political subdivisions, public higher-education institutions, wholly state-owned corporations, individual employees, and religious/sectarian organizations), "proper authorities", "protected person" (excluding managerial/executive/officer employees reporting within their job duties and reports made to the alleged wrongdoer), and "the motivating factor". Independent review revised heading to reflect all five defined terms and both employer and protected-person exclusions.

headings.title: Codification of at-will exceptions and exclusive statutory remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). States intent to codify existing common-law exceptions to at-will employment and limit future judicial expansion, and declares this section plus chapters 213 and 287 the exclusive remedy for unlawful employment practice claims.

headings.title: Prohibition on discharging protected persons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Makes discharging an individual defined as a protected person because of that status an unlawful employment practice.

headings.title: Private right of action for actual damages and statutory preclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Grants aggrieved protected persons a private right of action for actual damages (excluding punitive damages), but bars any private right of action under this statute if a private right of action for damages exists under another state or federal statutory or regulatory scheme.

headings.title: Right of any party to demand jury trial
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Permits any party to an action initiated under this section to demand a trial by jury.

headings.title: Exclusive remedies and liquidated damages under section 510.263
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Specifies court filing and restricts available remedies to back pay, directly related medical bill reimbursement, and double liquidated damages upon clear and convincing proof of outrageous employer conduct (evil motive or reckless indifference), applying § 510.263.

headings.title: Discretionary court costs and qualified attorney fee awards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43). Permits the court to award prevailing-party court costs and reasonable attorney fees in addition to subsection 7 damages, except that a prevailing respondent may receive attorney fees only upon showing the case was without foundation. Independent review revised heading to signal the "without foundation" restriction on prevailing-respondent attorney fee awards.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all eight subsections, subdivisions (2)(1)–(5) and (7)(1)–(3), and history note (L. 2017 S.B. 43); verified all fingerprints. Checked employer/public/religious and protected-person exclusions, at-will codification and chs. 213/287 exclusivity, statutory-remedy preclusion, jury demand, § 510.263 liquidated damages, and asymmetric respondent fee standard. Revised subsections 2 (all definitions and exclusions) and 8 (qualified attorney fee awards); retained subsections 1 and 3–7.

headings.title: Qualifying reasons for unpaid domestic or sexual violence leave
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) through (5), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Permits an employee who is a victim of domestic or sexual violence or has a non-adverse family/household member victim (retaining archived source phrasing) to take unpaid leave for medical care/recovery, victim services, psychological/other counseling, safety planning/relocation/economic security, or related legal assistance/proceedings.

headings.title: Leave duration by employer size and FMLA limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Subject to subsection 5, sets 12-month unpaid leave entitlements at two workweeks (50+ employees) or one workweek (20–49 employees), defines "workweek", prohibits reduction during the 12-month period, and specifies §§ 285.625 to 285.670 create no right to unpaid leave exceeding federal FMLA limits (29 U.S.C. § 2601 et seq.). Independent review revised heading from "cap" to "limit" to match statutory phrasing.

headings.title: Intermittent or reduced-schedule leave
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Allows leave described in subsection 2 to be taken intermittently or on a reduced work schedule.

headings.title: Advance notice and conditional protection for unscheduled absences
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Requires at least 48 hours' advance notice unless not practicable, and bars employer action for an unscheduled absence if the employee provides requested subsection 5 certification within a reasonable period. Independent review revised heading to reflect that unscheduled-absence protection is conditioned on providing requested subsection 5 certification.

headings.title: Employer requests for leave certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Permits an employer to require certification of victim status and qualifying subsection 1 purpose, to be provided by the employee within a reasonable period after request.

headings.title: Sworn statement and corroborating documentation for certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Allows satisfying subsection 5 certification with a sworn employee statement plus documentation from a victim services organization/attorney/clergy/medical or other professional, a police or court record, or other corroborating evidence.

headings.title: Confidentiality of leave records and disclosure exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Requires employers to retain subsection 6 submissions and the fact of requesting or obtaining leave in strictest confidence, except upon written employee request/consent or as required by federal or state law.

headings.title: Job restoration to same or equivalent position
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Entitles an employee returning from leave to restoration to the prior position or an equivalent position with equivalent benefits, pay, and other employment terms and conditions.

headings.title: Pre-leave benefits, accrual limits, and periodic status reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Protects pre-leave accrued employment benefits, disclaims seniority/benefit accrual during leave or enhanced restoration rights, and permits employers to require periodic status and return-intent reports during leave.

headings.title: Employer-requested certification for safety accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Requires an employee requesting a reasonable safety accommodation under §§ 285.625 to 285.670, upon employer request, to provide a signed written statement certifying an authorized purpose. Independent review revised heading to reflect that the signed written statement is required upon employer request.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all ten subsections, subdivisions (1)(1)–(5) and (6)(1)–(3), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432); verified all fingerprints. Checked archived victim/family wording in subsection 1, employer-size leave tiers and federal FMLA limit, certification conditions for unscheduled absences, confidentiality exceptions, restoration/accrual limits, and employer-requested safety-accommodation certification. Retained subsections 1, 3, and 5–9; revised subsections 2, 4, and 10 for statutory wording and qualifications.

headings.title: Continuation of group health coverage during leave
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Requires employers to maintain group health plan coverage for the employee and any family or household member during § 285.630 leave on the same level and conditions as continuous employment.

headings.title: Employer recovery of health premiums after nonreturn and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Permits an employer to recover premiums paid during leave if the employee fails to return after leave expires, except when nonreturn is due to continuation, recurrence, or onset of domestic violence, sexual violence, abuse, sexual assault, or human trafficking entitling leave under § 285.630 or other circumstances beyond the employee's control.

headings.title: Certification of inability to return to work
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) through (4), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Permits an employer to require reasonable-period certification from an employee claiming a subsection 2 exception via sworn statement, victim-services/attorney/clergy/medical or other professional documentation, police or court record, or other corroborating evidence. Independent review verified that subdivisions (1) through (4) are listed disjunctively ("or"), unlike § 285.630(6).

headings.title: Confidentiality of nonreturn records and disclosure exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Requires employers to keep subsection 3 information and the fact of nonreturn for a subsection 2 reason in strictest confidence, except upon written employee request/consent or as required by federal or state law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all four subsections, subdivisions (3)(1)–(4), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432); verified all fingerprints. Checked § 285.630 health-coverage continuation, premium-recovery exceptions, disjunctive ("or") certification options in subsection 3, and confidentiality exceptions. Retained all four headings as accurate.

headings.title: Reasonable safety accommodations by employers and public agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2) and nested paragraphs (a) and (b), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Requires employers (for employees) and public agencies (for public-assistance applicants or recipients) to make timely reasonable safety accommodations for known limitations of otherwise qualified individuals who are victims or have a non-adverse family/household member victim of domestic or sexual violence (retaining archived source trailing semicolon).

headings.title: Undue hardship exception to safety accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Exempts an employer or public agency from subsection 1 if it can demonstrate that the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on its operation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections, subdivisions (1)(1)–(2) and paragraphs (a)–(b), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed subsection 1 applies to both employers (for employees) and public agencies (for public-assistance applicants/recipients), noted archived trailing semicolon at end of subsection 1(2)(b), and checked undue-hardship exception in subsection 2. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Preservation of greater or broader leave benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Clarifies that §§ 285.625 to 285.670 do not supersede federal, state, or local laws, collective bargaining agreements, or benefit programs providing greater leave benefits or covering a larger population of victims.

headings.title: Protection against diminishment of statutory rights and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432). Provides that rights and remedies under §§ 285.625 to 285.670 for covered applicants and employees shall not be diminished by any federal, state, or local law, collective bargaining agreement, or employment benefits program or plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections, subdivisions (1)(1)–(2), and history note (L. 2021 H.B. 432); verified all fingerprints. Checked preservation of greater or broader leave benefits under §§ 285.625 to 285.670 and anti-diminishment protection for covered applicants and employees. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Short title as Professional Employer Organization Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Designates §§ 285.700 to 285.750 as the "Professional Employer Organization Act".

headings.title: Enforcement authority of secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Authorizes the secretary of state or a designee to enforce §§ 285.700 to 285.750.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719); verified all fingerprints. Checked §§ 285.700 to 285.750 short title and permissive enforcement authority of the secretary of state or designee. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Noninterference with collective bargaining and labor laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Clarifies that neither §§ 285.700 to 285.750 nor any professional employer agreement affects or modifies collective bargaining agreements or rights/obligations under the NLRA, Railway Labor Act, or §§ 105.500 to 105.530.

headings.title: Effect on employee rights, contracts, and restrictive covenants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Preserves pre-existing client-employee rights and obligations, preserves existing and subsequent contracts/restrictive covenants (without PEO liability unless agreed in writing), and creates no new enforceable employee rights against a PEO beyond the agreement and §§ 285.700 to 285.750. Independent review removed "existing" from heading because subdivision (2) also covers subsequent contracts/restrictive covenants and subdivision (3) bars new enforceable rights against a PEO.

headings.title: Preservation of client and employee licensing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Provides that neither §§ 285.700 to 285.750 nor any professional employer agreement modifies federal, state, or local licensing, registration, or certification requirements for clients or covered employees.

headings.title: Sole client-employee status for licensed covered employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Deems covered employees required to be licensed, registered, or certified to be solely employees of the client for those requirements.

headings.title: PEO not deemed engaged in regulated occupations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Provides that a PEO is not deemed to engage in a licensed, registered, certified, or regulated occupation or trade solely by coemploying a regulated covered employee.

headings.title: Client control over licensed activities and continued regulation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Reserves sole direction and control of covered employees' professional/licensed activities and client business to the client, while keeping clients and covered employees subject to regulatory oversight.

headings.title: Client eligibility for employment-based tax credits and incentives
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Deems covered employees solely client employees for government employment-based tax credits, incentives, and benefits regardless of PEO W-2 reporting, limits headcounts to the client's own coemployed workers, and requires PEOs to furnish supporting employment data upon client or state agency request.

headings.title: Preservation of minority and women's business enterprise status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Protects a client company's § 37.020 minority or women's business enterprise certification for state or political subdivision bids, contracts, purchase orders, or agreements from being affected by using a PEO.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all eight subsections, subdivisions (2)(1)–(3), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719); verified all fingerprints. Checked NLRA/RLA/§§ 105.500–105.530 labor-law preservation, existing and subsequent contracts/restrictive covenants and no-new-PEO-rights rule in subsection 2, licensing rules, tax-credit eligibility, and § 37.020 MBE/WBE status. Revised subsection 2 to remove "existing"; retained subsections 1 and 3–8.

headings.title: Registration prerequisite for providing or advertising PEO services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Prohibits providing, advertising, or holding oneself out as providing professional employer services in Missouri without registration under §§ 285.700 to 285.750, except as otherwise provided.

headings.title: Required registration application information and financial audits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (7), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Lists registration disclosures to the secretary of state—business names, principal/Missouri addresses, tax/EIN, five-year jurisdictional name/predecessor/successor history, 25%+ ownership statement, senior management statement, and GAAP CPA-audited going-concern financial statements (13-month initial audit, 180-day annual audit with extension procedure, consolidated option, and CPA-reviewed fallback for <12 months operating history).

headings.title: Initial registration deadlines and interim operating permits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Sets the 180-day post-August 28, 2018 initial registration deadline and validity period for existing Missouri PEOs, requires pre-operation registration for new PEOs, sets a five-business-day notice and limited/full registration rule when an unregistered PEO learns an out-of-state client has Missouri employees, and authorizes discretionary interim operating permits for out-of-state licensed PEOs.

headings.title: Annual registration renewal and continued validity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires annual renewal within 180 days after fiscal year-end by reporting information changes and keeps existing registration in effect while renewal is pending.

headings.title: Combined or consolidated reporting and PEO group guarantees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Permits PEO groups to satisfy reporting and financial requirements on a combined or consolidated basis if group members mutually guarantee financial capacity obligations and, when non-PEO entities are included in consolidated statements, the controlling entity guarantees PEO group obligations.

headings.title: Eligibility, duration, documentation, and exemptions for limited registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, including subdivisions (1) through (4) and paragraphs (a) through (d), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Sets four eligibility criteria for limited registration (application form, out-of-state domicile/licensure, no Missouri office or direct solicitation, <=50 Missouri covered employees on any day), one-year renewable validity, documentation requirements, and exemption from § 285.725.

headings.title: Public list of registered professional employer organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Directs the secretary of state to maintain a publicly accessible electronic or other list of registered PEOs.

headings.title: Secretary of state authority to produce forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Permits the secretary of state to produce forms necessary for efficient administration of this section.

headings.title: Electronic filings and optional approved assurance organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Directs practical acceptance of electronic filings under §§ 432.200 to 432.295, allows optional PEO compliance/filings/fee payment through secretary-of-state-approved assurance organizations (including in lieu of §§ 285.715 and 285.725 requirements), and preserves SOS registration, termination, investigation, and enforcement authority.

headings.title: Confidentiality of PEO filings under section 610.010 and exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Makes all records, reports, and information obtained from a PEO under §§ 285.700 to 285.750 confidential and outside the § 610.010 definition of "public record", except as necessary for SOS administration. Independent review revised heading to reflect the secretary-of-state administrative exception.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all ten subsections, all subdivisions and paragraphs, and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719); verified all fingerprints. Checked August 28, 2018 initial registration deadlines, CPA audit/extension/review rules, PEO group guarantees, <=50-employee limited registration and § 285.725 exemption, optional approved assurance organizations under §§ 432.200 to 432.295, and § 610.010 confidentiality exception for SOS administration. Retained subsections 1–9; revised subsection 10 to include the administrative exception.

headings.title: Initial registration fee limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Caps a PEO's initial registration fee under §§ 285.700 to 285.750 at $500.

headings.title: Annual renewal fee limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Caps a PEO's annual registration renewal fee under §§ 285.700 to 285.750 at $250.

headings.title: Fee determination for group registrations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Directs the secretary of state to determine any fee charged for a group registration.

headings.title: Limited registration initial and renewal fee limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Caps limited registration fees at $250 upon initial application and upon each renewal.

headings.title: Reasonable administrative cost cap on fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Prohibits any fee charged under §§ 285.700 to 285.750 from exceeding the amount reasonably necessary to administer those sections.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all five subsections and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719); verified all fingerprints. Checked $500 initial and $250 renewal/limited caps, SOS group-fee determination, and reasonable administrative-cost ceiling across §§ 285.700 to 285.750. Retained all five headings as accurate.

headings.title: Default allocation of client and PEO rights and duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400). Except as provided by statute or agreement, assigns general employer rights/duties and exclusive operational/fiduciary/licensure control to the client while limiting PEO coemployer rights and duties to statutory and agreement terms during coemployment.

headings.title: Required professional employer agreement terms and wage definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (3), paragraphs (a) through (c), and the continuation paragraph defining "wages", and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400). Requires agreements to allocate subsection 1 duties, obligate the PEO to pay wages, handle payroll/unemployment taxes, and pay assumed benefits (excluding bonuses, commissions, severance, deferred compensation, profit sharing, and PTO from "wages" unless expressly assumed), and define PEO and client hiring, discipline, and termination rights.

headings.title: Written notice of coemployment to covered employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400). Requires a PEO to give each affected covered employee written notice of the general nature of the coemployment relationship.

headings.title: Default liability allocation and insurance exclusion rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, including subdivisions (1) through (6), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400). Unless agreed otherwise, assigns product/service quality and work supervision solely to the client, sets mutual nonliability for acts under the other coemployer's express direction, preserves written contractual liabilities, and excludes covered employees from PEO general/fidelity/surety/non-workers'-compensation/liquor policies unless specifically included.

headings.title: Benefit plan sponsorship, insurance status, and section 375.014
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400). Clarifies that PEOs are not selling insurance or acting as third-party administrators, deems both clients and registered PEOs employers for retirement and welfare benefit plans, treats fully insured PEO welfare plans as single-employer plans, deems registered PEOs employers of all participating clients' eligible covered employees for health plans, and preserves § 375.014 without superseding or preempting it.

headings.title: State and local gross-receipts, per-employee, and payroll taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400). Sets state and political-subdivision tax rules: gross-receipts deductions for pass-through wages/benefits/payroll taxes, per-capita/per-employee assessments against clients for covered employees (with credit for PEO-provided mandate benefits) and against PEOs for non-covered staff, and PEO eligibility to apply client small-business allowances/exemptions on total-payroll taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all six subsections, all subdivisions/paragraphs, the subsection 2 continuation paragraph defining "wages", and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719, A.L. 2022 H.B. 2400); verified all fingerprints. Checked default coemployer/liability allocations, required agreement terms and wage exclusions, insurance/TPA/welfare-plan rules preserving § 375.014, and state/local tax deductions and assessments. Retained all six headings as accurate.

headings.title: Contractual allocation of workers' compensation coverage responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires the professional employer agreement to allocate responsibility for obtaining compliant workers' compensation coverage for covered employees to either the client or the PEO.

headings.title: Voluntary and residual market coverage options and self-insured reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (3), paragraphs (a) and (b), and the continuation paragraph after (2)(b), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires a client's direct and covered employees to be all in the voluntary or all in the residual market with the same carrier; lists voluntary-market options (client policy or § 287.280 self-insurance; PEO § 287.280 self-insurance, 20 CSR 500-6.800(5)(c)2 policy, or multiple coordinated policy); requires § 287.280 self-insured PEOs to report client experience-rating data; and lists residual-market policy options.

headings.title: Experience modification data maintained by voluntary-market PEOs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) through (4), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires voluntary-market PEOs to maintain and furnish insurers client corporate name, tax/EIN, payroll summaries/class codes (and employee lists on request), and client-grouped claims data for post-termination experience modification calculations, while continuing to use term data in future PEO ratings.

headings.title: Policy cancellation grounds, ten-day client notice, and exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Makes material violations grounds for policy cancellation or nonrenewal in addition to chapter 287, and requires PEOs to notify covered clients by certified mail within 10 days of receiving cancellation/nonrenewal notice unless an authorized-carrier replacement policy takes effect on the same date. Independent review revised heading to include the same-date replacement policy notice exception and noted archived phrasing "any material violations ... is grounds".

headings.title: Post-termination experience rating, data transfer, and insurer notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Directs terminated clients to use individual experience modification factors, requires PEOs to furnish subsection 3 data to clients within five business days of termination notice and to future insurers on client request, and requires insurer notice prior to termination when feasible or within five business days after.

headings.title: Coemployer status and exclusive remedy under chapter 287
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Deems both client and PEO employers under chapter 287, extends § 287.120 exclusive-remedy protection to the PEO, client, and all employees regardless of which party obtains coverage, and clarifies neither party is exempt from chapter 287 compliance.

headings.title: Client right to experience data within five business days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Allows a client to request subsection 3 experience data at any time and requires the PEO to provide it within five business days. Independent review revised heading to specify five business days rather than five days.

headings.title: Third-party requests for experience data and client consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). For 20 CSR 500-6.800(5)(c)2 policies, requires a PEO to furnish only subsection 3 data to a requesting third party within five business days after client consent (retaining archived source phrasing "of receipt of receiving the client's consent"), or to notify the third party if the client refuses consent.

headings.title: Client duty to give prospective insurers PEO experience data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires a client to provide prospective insurers with subsection 3 data upon receipt from the PEO and makes failure a violation of § 287.128(6).

headings.title: Client duty to disclose PEO relationships and coverage exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires clients to notify prospective insurers of previous or current PEO relationships (with failure violating § 287.128(6)), unless the PEO did not provide workers' compensation coverage during coemployment.

headings.title: Registered PEO unemployment status under chapter 288
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Directs that a PEO registered under §§ 285.700 to 285.750 be treated as a lesser employing unit under § 288.032 for chapter 288 unemployment compensation purposes. Independent review revised heading to make chapter 288 unemployment status explicit within a workers'-compensation-titled section.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all 11 subsections, all subdivisions/paragraphs, the subsection 2 continuation paragraph on § 287.280 self-insured PEO reporting, and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719); verified all fingerprints. Checked 20 CSR 500-6.800(5)(c)2 references, § 287.120 exclusive remedy, § 287.128(6) disclosure violations, archived wording in subsections 4 ("violations ... is") and 8 ("of receipt of receiving the client's consent"), and subsection 11's chapter 288 / § 288.032 unemployment status inside a workers'-compensation-titled section. Retained eight headings; revised subsections 4 (replacement-policy notice exception), 7 (five business days), and 11 (explicit chapter 288 unemployment status).

headings.title: Prohibited knowing unregistered PEO services and false filings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) and (2), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Prohibits knowingly offering/providing PEO services or using PEO, staff-leasing, employee-leasing, administrative-employer, or similar titles without registration, or providing false or fraudulent registration, renewal, or report information to the secretary of state. Independent review revised heading to reflect knowing unregistered PEO services and false filings, matching statutory "registered" terminology in subsection 1 (while subsections 2–3 refer to "licensee"/"license").

headings.title: Grounds for mandatory disciplinary action by secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (3), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Requires secretary of state disciplinary action for operation-related criminal convictions of a PEO or controlling person, knowing material misrepresentations to the secretary of state or another government agency, or willful violations of §§ 285.700 to 285.750 or an SOS order.

headings.title: Hearing, appeal, and discretionary disciplinary sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) through (5), and history note (L. 2018 H.B. 1719). Authorizes the secretary of state, after notice, hearing opportunity, finding of violation, and subject to appeal, to deny a license, revoke/restrict/refuse renewal, impose an administrative penalty up to $1,000 per material violation, place the licensee on probation with conditions, or issue a cease and desist order.

Checked knowing unregistered services/false-filing prohibitions in subsection 1, mandatory disciplinary grounds in subsection 2, hearing/appeal prerequisites and discretionary sanctions in subsection 3, and archived shift from "registered" (subsection 1) to "licensee"/"license" (subsections 2–3). Revised subsection 1 to reflect knowing unregistered PEO services and false filings; retained subsections 2–3.
